- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model fails to capture sharp downward momentum, often lagging by 1–3 days.
- Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next period; if below, adjust up by 5–10%.
- Avoid overreacting to sentiment spikes: if sentiment turns sharply positive, reduce forecast magnitude by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate — apply upward bias of 3–7% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Correct for “overshoot after spike” — if price spiked > 5% in last 3 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.
